user.title: Connect a CMR controller
user.description: Home Assistant reads the controller's CMR menus over the router's REST API. Create a user group with the `read`, `api` and `rest-api` policies (add `write` to start upgrades from Home Assistant) and enable `www-ssl` (or `www` with HTTPS off).

data_description.host: IP address or host name of the router running the CMR controller, optionally with :port.
data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off for the router's self-signed certificate.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to {host} again
reauth_confirm.description: The controller rejected the saved credentials.

reconfigure.title: Change the controller connection
reconfigure.description: New address, user or HTTPS settings for the same controller. To connect a different controller, add a new entry instead.

data_description.host: IP address or host name, optionally with :port.
data_description.password: Leave empty to keep the saved password.

error.cannot_connect: Can't reach the REST API. Check the address, that the www-ssl (or www) service is enabled, and the HTTPS setting. {detail}
error.invalid_auth: The controller rejected the login, or the user's group lacks the read, api and rest-api policies. {detail}
error.no_cmr: This router has no /cmr menu. Install the cmr package and enable the controller. Router said: {detail}
error.not_controller: The router has a /cmr menu but isn't acting as a CMR controller.

abort.already_configured: This controller is already set up.
abort.wrong_controller: That address answers as a different controller. Add it as a new entry; this one stays with its controller.

create_entry.default: Reload this browser page (Ctrl+F5 / Cmd+Shift+R) so the CMR cards and the *CMR network* dashboard become available, then add it under Settings → Dashboards → Add dashboard.

init.title: CMR options
init.description:
To get alerts in Home Assistant the moment they fire, run this on the controller. It points every alert rule's HTTP action at Home Assistant; edit `find` to limit it to some rules.

```
{script}
```

data.webhook_base_url: Home Assistant address, as the controller reaches it
data.allow_upgrades: Allow actions on the controller (upgrades, pairing)

data_description.allow_upgrades: Adds Install to each firmware update, a button per upgrade rule, and Approve for devices waiting to be paired. Needs the `write` policy on the router user.
data_description.activity_log: Which controller events also appear in Home Assistant's activity log. The integration's own timeline always keeps everything.
data_description.catalog_url: Optional. A product catalog that adds photos and product names to devices; leave empty to turn it off. Photos then load from the catalog's image server.

detection.name: Issue detection
detection.description: How many occurrences inside a rule's time window raise an issue. 0 turns a rule off.

error.catalog_empty: The product catalog returned no products with photos.

device_gone.message: The controller no longer manages this item.

no_newer_version.message: {device} is on {version}; its channel offers nothing newer.

rule_would_downgrade.message: Not running {rule}: its channel would move {devices} to an older version.

rule_nothing_to_do.message: Every device in {rule} is already up to date.

options.notable: Notable events (devices, upgrades, alerts, security, config changes, issues)
options.all: All events, including every Wi-Fi join and link change

network_issue.title: {title}
network_issue.description:
{detail}

This was detected by the CMR integration and clears itself once things are quiet again.

pairing_pending.title: {identity} is waiting to be paired
pairing_pending.description: A {board} has connected to the controller and waits for approval there. Approve it here, or run `/cmr/device/pair` for it on the controller. Approving from Home Assistant needs *Allow actions on the controller* in the integration's options.

confirm.title: Approve pairing of {identity}
confirm.description: The controller will accept {identity} ({board}) as a managed device. Only when the device itself requires a password, enter the credentials of a user on that device; otherwise leave both empty.

abort.not_pending: This device is no longer waiting for approval.

pairing_remote.title: {identity} is waiting for approval on the device
pairing_remote.description: The controller accepted the {board} but the device's own pairing requirement is not met yet. Run `/cmr/client/pair` on the device (with the controller's credentials if it asks for a password). This notice disappears once the pairing completes.
